summary: Accepted the separate critic's supported verdict for the pointwise contamination bound, exceptional term at most 3, fixed-epsilon consequence, adaptive-epsilon counterexample, and supplemental endpoint identities. Preserved all reviewed originals and added a dated erratum: strict quarter-root roughness admits at most three prime factors, not four; triples still make the P/S four-cell model nonexhaustive. Recorded handwritten proof plus separate host-agent review and independent finite checks, with no formal or external peer verification and no novelty claim. Added an elementary conditional linear-margin implication: a uniform-in-epsilon c*epsilon lower margin for F would dominate the proved C*epsilon^2 contamination after choosing one fixed epsilon<c/C, but that lower input remains unproved and may be harder than the original one-epsilon P-open condition. Goldbach and the substantive parity-sensitive lower-bound objective remain unresolved.

claims.text: The reviewed uniform pointwise H bound and its fixed-epsilon consequence are accepted with exceptional term omega_{>N^alpha}(N)<=3, absolute unspecified constants and the stated assurance limits.
The inherited claim permitting four prime factors at the strict quarter-root roughness cutoff is false; at most three factors can survive below N.

Assuming a c*epsilon pointwise liminf lower margin for F at every sufficiently small fixed epsilon, with c independent of epsilon, the reviewed H bound implies Goldbach for all sufficiently large even targets.
Neither the sufficient P-open lower estimate nor the stronger uniform linear-margin lower input is proved in this investigation.
Novelty, numerical effective sieve constants, an explicit all-target threshold, and external peer or formal verification remain unestablished.
